Her young nephew Aro watched with wide eyes. "Aunt, why do you always give everything? What if one day the keeper keeps it all?"

"Then the tablet will remember," Liss said, "and so will I. But look how rarely that happens.

When the young keepers asked what ruled the lake, Sela pointed to its eight reflections. “The water multiplies what we risk,” she said, “but our choices decide where the warmth goes. Give freely, share enough to reward courage, and do not mistake a blurred crossing for a cold heart.”

The heron of Want perched between the lanterns. “Keep everything when the harvest comes,” it croaked. “Tomorrow you may never meet this keeper again.”

The moon answered from the water: “A stranger does not need your name to remember a generous shore.”
